name: Curry Leaf
hook: Curry leaf dropping its leaves in winter? It's too cold.

steps.title: Sun, with summer shade
steps.tip: Give it full sun in a sheltered spot, but shade it from harsh summer sun so the leaves don't scorch.

steps.title: Let it dry between drinks
steps.tip: Water when the soil has dried out, and use a fast-draining pot so the roots never sit wet.

steps.title: Indoors before frost
steps.tip: It can't survive freezing and drops leaves in the cold. Bring the pot inside for winter.

steps.title: Acidic to neutral soil
steps.tip: Use potting soil that holds some moisture but drains well. It should be acidic to neutral, not alkaline.

steps.title: Pick leaves, skip berries
steps.tip: Pick fresh leaves any time and trim to keep it compact. Avoid the berries: the seeds are considered toxic.

steps.title: Check for mites and scale
steps.tip: Look under the leaves for spider mites, scale insects and mealybugs, especially indoors.

outro: Sun, dry soil between waterings and a warm winter: fresh leaves.

faqs.question: Should I dry curry leaves to store them?
faqs.answer: Fresh leaves have the best flavor, and drying loses much of it. Freeze extra leaves instead.
